assessment: The revolver worries me more than the DSCR. The utilization trend is linear, not seasonal, and they are using the revolver to cover operating cash shortfalls. If it slips again, the revolver becomes a problem before the aerospace business arrives. On aerospace, we have believed the recovery story twice, and it has moved twice. We have asked twice for the purchase order and received nothing, and the answer on the 1/23 call felt evasive. We can't keep accepting verbal assurances. David is cooperative and doesn't hide bad news, but he delivers it late and without the documentation. The business is sound, and the auto headwind is sector-wide; this is not a management quality problem. If aerospace delivers as now represented and auto stabilizes, DSCR could get to 1.15-1.20x by Q3. I want to see documentation before underwriting that again. The credit has moved into territory where we need more information and more frequent visibility.
recommendation: I am not recommending a second waiver now. I recommend we hold the existing waiver and set a February 14 deadline for (1) the aerospace purchase order, (2) 12-month cash flow projections with assumptions, and (3) names on the 60-90 day accounts receivable. If these arrive and support the recovery, I will come back with a recommendation to extend the waiver. I also recommend restricting revolver draws above 75% utilization pending review; utilization is at 69% now.

questions_for_rm: In "problem before aerospace arrives if it slips again," does "it" refer to the aerospace timing? I kept it as "if it slips again" so I would not assume the referent.
The notes do not say what happens if the February 14 items do not arrive, or if they arrive but do not support the recovery. Do you want to state a next step for that case?
"More frequent visibility": do you want to specify the reporting cadence or which items you need, such as monthly financials or borrowing base reporting?
"Restrict revolver draws above 75% utilization pending review": which review do you mean, and when is it expected to conclude?
The note line on the waiver extension included a redacted internal classification reference (policy 2.1). I left it out of the memo. Should a classification reference be added before this goes out?
Which covenant does the existing waiver cover? The notes do not name it, so the memo refers only to "the existing waiver."
